newsitem.title: GREECE: Tension rises as Greek seamen continue blockade.
newsitem.headline: Tension rises as Greek seamen continue blockade.

text.p: Seamen were striking for a fifth day on Friday, blocking ships and ferries all over Greece and causing major problems in transportation of both passengers and fresh agricultural goods, radio stations reported.
Seamen demonstrated early in the day in Piraeus, protesting against unemployment, wage cuts, higher taxes and insufficient insurance and pension programmes.
The Panhellenic Seamen's Federation (PNO) said it was particularly upset about government plans to abolish special tax exemptions that were provided to seamen for a period of almost 40 years.
National economy deputy minister George Drys and merchant marine minister Stavros Soumakis met PNO representatives as well as the union of Coastal Shipowners to discuss seamen's demands.
The government has pledged to try to find a solution with the unions by January 7 and will present the proposals to parliament, the national economy ministry said in a statement.
PNO said it would meet to decide whether this was sufficient to call off its strike.
Seamen have been blocking the country's ports since Monday, with the exception of Kavala in the north. The seamen are supported by shipowners who are opposed to paying higher taxes.

Greece, which has been paralysed by farmers' road blockades for 23 days, faces the prospect of shortages of essential goods if the seamen and farmers keep up their actions. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
